messages:
OncallBot: incident-bot detected canary healthcheck spike for rollout edge-2026-03-14 in us-west-2. metric: canary_5xx_rate > 15% over 2m. PagerDuty page fired to #oncall-inference. auto-escalation in 5m if unacked.
PagerDuty: INC-20260314-1 triggered (canary-failure-high-5xx-rate). Triage level: P1. Affected service: inference-api (canary pool). PagerDuty: page sent to Incident Response rotation.
Alice M: saw the alert in dashboards — looks correlated with the 1.3.4 canary rollout that started ~09:42 UTC. Canary nodes showing 503/504. Not all regions, mainly us-west-2. Notified product leads.
Ben R: ACK. I'm oncall. Pulling logs + request ids. Can someone paste the canary rollout id?
Carla S: rollout id: rollout-edge-1.3.4-20260314-0918. Canary subset: inference-edge-canary-1..4.
Ben R: thanks. Running quick sanity: 
```bash
# hit canary directly
curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null -X POST https://inference-canary-usw2.internal/api/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```
Ben R: getting 503s with upstream error: "kv-cache-miss timeout" in logs. stack shows attempts to fetch prefix cache from kvstore timed out.
Priya K: hitting the same in our smoke runner. Error rate on canary instances jumped at 09:44 right after model shard rollout. Could be cache sharding change in 1.3.4.
PagerDuty: 2 minutes elapsed — no ack from primary responder, escalated to L2 oncall (Ben R).
Ben R: I'll try to roll the canary back to 1.3.3 for now, and pause the rollout. Plan: 1) pause rollout traffic 2) rollback canary 3) watch metrics 4) if stable, stop the staged rollout. Any objections?
Emily J: no objections. We should announce customer-impact window (internal) and check Dedicated customers pinned to this model.
Ben R: executing rollback now:
```bash
kubectl -n inference rollout undo deployment/inference-edge --to-revision=42  # previous stable 1.3.3
kubectl -n inference scale deployment/inference-edge-canary --replicas=0  # drain canary
```
OncallBot: deploy-bot: rollback job submitted for deployment/inference-edge to revision=42 by Ben R. Watch logs at https://deploys.internal/logs/rollback-2460001234.
OncallBot: PagerDuty check-in: "ack" recorded by Ben R at 2460001240. Auto-escalation suspended.
Carla S: paused rollout in console and removed canary traffic weights. Notifying infra to watch kvstore cluster (kv-primary-usw2).
Shawn L: infra here — observed increased latency/queue depth on kv-primary-usw2 around 09:44. We saw connection saturation from the canary pool, likely due to small change in async prefetch behavior. Rolling a small config tweak to raise connection pools and bump timeouts while rollback completes.
Ben R: after rollback started, 5xx rate dropped from 17% -> 4% in 3 minutes on global ingress metrics. Still seeing a few stragglers for ~10m.
Priya K: customer-impact check: estimated affected QPS ~120 requests/min for that canary cohort, ~0.8% of total global traffic. No external SLA breaches observed yet but could have impacted a small set of users routed to us-west-2. Logging flagged a handful of paid customers with errors; CS alerted.
PagerDuty: escalation timer cleared. Incident severity remains P1 until confirmed stable for 30m.
Ben R: running canary healthcheck script against control plane and kvstore, returning OK for all endpoints now.
Carla S: note for follow-up — model shard mapping in 1.3.4 changed KV prefixing. Need regression test to simulate cache cold-start under sharded config.
Emily J: opened a bug: INF-8732 "canary kv prefixing regression in 1.3.4" and assigned to eng-runtime. Added repro steps and link to logs.
Ben R: documenting immediate mitigation in this thread and preparing to hand off to SRE for monitoring and postmortem. Next actions:
- Shawn L to monitor kvstore and confirm no residual saturation.
- Priya K to run canary smoke suite on staging 1.3.4 with kvstore-limited env.
- Carla S to coordinate rollback announcement and update on-call doc.
- Ben R to close pager after 30m stable window.
Shawn L: kv metrics falling back to normal. Connection queue at 12% of capacity now. No retry storms observed.
Priya K: repro in staging reproduced — small change in prefetch batch size causes heavy connection churn under concurrent prefetche requests. Raising default pool and adding jitter fixes it. Will open PR.
OncallBot: PagerDuty incident INC-20260314-1 status: acknowledged by Ben R at 2460001240, mitigated at 2460001480 (observed reduction in 5xx rate), will auto-resolve at 2460001600 if no regressions.
Ben R: marking the incident mitigated. Adding short notes: cause: shard-aware kv prefixing + prefetch change in 1.3.4 caused connection saturation in us-west-2 under canary traffic. Mitigation: rollback to 1.3.3, pause rollout, connection pool bump and jitter in staging. Impact: transient 5xx rise ~17% on canary cohort (~0.8% global) affecting a handful of paid customers (CS notified).
Alice M: thanks everyone for quick response. Please make sure the postmortem includes why the rollout change wasn't caught by the canary smoke tests and add a test for kv cold-start under sharded configs.
Emily J: assigning postmortem lead to Ben R and eng-runtime. Will schedule RCA meeting and notify relevant stakeholders.
Ben R: closing pager now; will re-open if we see recurrence. :thumbsup: :ambulance:
OncallBot: PagerDuty: INC-20260314-1 auto-resolved at 2460001600.
